newsitem.title: UK: Rosy yen charts add weight to bullish outlook.
newsitem.headline: Rosy yen charts add weight to bullish outlook.

text.p: Technical analysts are joining the chorus of yen bulls as charts paint a rosy outlook for the Japanese currency against its major counterparts.
Buoyed by the perfect combination of positive fundamentals and bright chart outlooks, the yen sliced through key resistance levels against the dollar, the mark, the Swiss franc and sterling.
Any consolidation is likely to add extra fuel for an extension of its rally, analysts said.
"The charts clearly point to further yen strength across the board," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.

Many chartists expect the mark to be the main victim of the yen's strength. On Monday, mark/yen fell to a 21-month low at 65.22, down some 13 percent from its 1997 peak at 75.09, set in early February. At 1210 GMT it was at 65.63/64.
Dollar/yen slumped to a six-month low at 111.80 on Monday, down 12.3 percent from its 1997 high at 127.46, set on May 1. It traded at 112.37/40 at the European midsession.
Sterling/yen on Monday also fell to its lowest level since December last year at 183.11, before recovering to 184.19/47 on Tuesday.
Swiss franc/yen pushed below 80 for the first time since August 1995, and chartists said it is poised to target the 75 area in the medium-term from its current level of 78.45/55.
Further yen gains against the dollar are expected to target the 111.80 level again in the short-term, with a move through the psychologically-important 110 level seen heralding a sharp sell-off.

"The dollar's move below 115 has signalled a potential bear flag formation, and a move below 111.85 would confirm that," said Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank of America. Erosion of Monday's low would set up the next target at 108 and then at 106, he added.
Jones at CSFB said the dollar's rally back above 112 yen on Tuesday was only corrective. Her short-term target is 109.20 to 108.80.
The 109.20 area marks a 38.2 Fibonacci retracement of the dollar's entire move from record lows at 79.76 in April 1995 to the 1997 high.

"The 108.80 level, a breakup point on the downside, is expected to yield," said Jones. Below there, the next target is at 104.40, and possibly 103.70/60, a 50 percent retracement of the upmove, she said.
Mark/yen is on course for a test of the psychologically-important 65 level, a strong support on the medium-term charts.
A break below 65.20 support would trigger a sharp sell-off to the lower boundary of a long-term ascending trend channel intervening at 63.05, said Hans-Gunther Redeker, technical analyst at Chase.
A decline below that major support would put the lows of autumn 1994 around 58.80 into focus, he added.
Fibonacci support at 64.55 yen - a 61.8 percent retracement of the move from 57.55 to 75.87 - might save the mark for now but the topside looks heavy above 67.
"There is a retracement band between 64.80 and 64.55, and while I expect the mark to hold at that level initially, I think it will drop to 63 and then 61.45 eventually," said Jones.
Swiss franc/yen is expected to slip further after eroding the 80 level last week. The cross is on course for a test of key support at 75.45, from 78.45/55 at present, said Jones.
The 75.45/80 area marks a 61.8 percent retracement of the move from the August 1993 at 66.05 to the November 1995 high at 91.45.
Dunne at Bank of America also said Swiss/yen was bound to target support at 75.40 and then 75.00.
